Mitchell carries Natal separately: its `natal` label has nine items 1852-1909 (maize, tobacco, livestock) and NO sugar cane, and its `cape of good hope` label has tobacco only, so the pre-Union cane series exists only under `south africa`, the label every other pre-1910 item routes to the Cape through. The series runs straight into the Union's across 1910 (21,000 ha at 1907 -> 26,000 ha at 1910; 79,000 t at 1909 -> 72,000 t at 1910), and the Union's cane is Natal's. No collision: `natal` has no sugar-cane cell in any year, so nothing is double counted.

Same agronomy as the Mitchell cane rows: sugar was grown only in Natal before Union. IIA's 1909 `south africa` raw sugar (74,171 t) continues its own Union series (72,241 t at 1910, 86,871 t at 1911), so whichever territory IIA meant for 1909 -- the colony or a Union back-cast -- the sugar is Natal's. The other 1909 IIA `south africa` rows (cotton lint) are NOT relabelled: no item-specific evidence places them.

STRUCTURAL, FROM AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE. fao1952 `Union of South Africa` horses read 778 thousand at 1937 -- equal to Mitchell's own `south africa` 1937 horses (778,000), which identifies the column -- and 679 thousand at 1950, equal to this label's 1949 figure (679,000) and within 0.5% of its 1950 one (676,000). Mitchell's `south africa` has no horse value in 1938-1958, exactly the years `natal` fills, and the `natal` values run continuously from the national 778,000 (1937) to 472,000 (1959). Natal's own pre-Union count was 40,000-67,000 over 1900-1908. The 1957 `natal` pig value (16,000) sits BESIDE a real `south africa` pig value, so it is not this shape and is not relabelled; it stays unrouted.

FILING, NOT MAGNITUDE ALONE. fao1952's land table files these two 1951 `New Guinea` rows under ASIA, the continent under which it files every `Netherlands New Guinea` row (cropa 1949-1950, population 1951); every other fao1952 `New Guinea` row (rubber, copra, cacao, tractors, population) is under OCEANIA. The Australian territories' own 1951 land use is carried separately, as `New Guinea and Papua` (use total 47,400 thousand ha). The stated 41,278 thousand ha (412,780 km2) is also 1.006x NNG-1949-1963's polygon (410,361 km2) against 1.74x TNGU-1949-1975's (237,462).
